GracePrinciples.Principle: GRACE 4 current project state lives under .grace and future agents should treat .grace as durable project context.
Contract-first changes: clarify purpose, scope, inputs, outputs, acceptance, and verification before implementation unless the user asks for a bounded direct fix.
Use the smallest correct change that satisfies the request and preserve repository terminology.
Keep semantic anchors stable and grep-friendly. File-local anchors include START_MODULE_CONTRACT, START_MODULE_MAP, START_CONTRACT, START_BLOCK, and START_CHANGE_SUMMARY.
Semantic GRACE anchors are XML tags, never attributes. Module IDs use M-*, data flows use DF-*, graph documents use GD-*, verification entries use V-M-*, and change bundles use C-*.
src is the source of truth for code behavior; dist is generated output and is never edited manually.
Config safety matters: writes must be conservative, idempotent, scope-aware, and must never silently clobber user-owned config.
Verification is a first-class artifact. Completion claims require fresh evidence from deterministic tests, typecheck, lint, build, pack, release, or GRACE checks as applicable.
Public CLI commands, package exports, config paths, and setup behavior are user-facing contracts; update README and current .grace artifacts when they change.
Invalid existing user config should fail with clear diagnostics before mutation rather than being silently repaired.
Workflow automation uses explicit work-item IDs and simple counters, not semantic clustering or fuzzy similarity.
NEEDS_CONTEXT and BLOCKED statuses halt automation and return control to the main session or user.
Repository memory and generated summaries must never override explicit user instructions, code, tests, README, or current .grace state.
Create C-* change bundles only for active approved GRACE work; do not create retroactive C-* bundles for completed work.

Plans that modify existing behavior require machine-checkable content baselines; an existence-only baseline is sufficient only when PlanningNotes explicitly justify why stronger behavioral drift detection is not meaningful.
Archived C-* specifications and plans are immutable historical evidence and must not be retrofitted solely to satisfy planning or assertion policies introduced later.

vv-opencode is a portable methodology for disciplined agentic development with a concrete runtime implementation as OpenCode plugins. The host runtime owns streaming, model invocation, sandboxing, and permission mechanics; vv-opencode supplies the discipline above them. Mechanical enforcement concentrates in the hook-backed plugins (workflow state machine, hashline edit, secrets redaction, Guardian permission auto-approval); the rest of the method is prompt-level guidance.
